names.source: registration app_command_init.cpp:284, spelling base_command_interface.hpp:544, case app_command_interface.cpp:1833 -> coreLink.cpp:142-144 -> skyline_mgr.cpp:144-154 -> SkyLine_Precession built at skyline_mgr.cpp:394, drawn skyline.cpp:1372-1464 with the year labels at skyline.cpp:1423-1447
names.notes: Two circles are drawn, one around each ecliptic pole. The labels are calendar years every thousand years. Earth only (skyline.cpp:1378).

names.name: text_usr_color
names.doc: The colour given to text put on the dome from now on when the text command names no colour of its own.
names.source: registration app_command_init.cpp:285, spelling base_command_interface.hpp:545, case app_command_interface.cpp:1834 -> Media::textSetDefaultColor media.hpp:338-340 -> TextMgr::setColor text_mgr.cpp:130-133 (writes defaultTextColor), consumed when a text is created at text_mgr.cpp:118-125
names.notes: Belongs to the `text` command (app_command_interface.cpp:2813-2837), NOT to `print`: `print` only writes its arguments to the log and draws nothing (app_command_interface.cpp:2096-2110). The colour is copied into each text as it is created, so texts already on the dome keep the colour they were given. It is also the only colour besides star_table with no getter anywhere in the tree (app_command_interface.cpp:1841-1844), so a saved session cannot read it back.

names.name: star_table
names.doc: The colour used for stars of one shade; index picks the shade, 0 for the bluest through 127 for the reddest.
names.source: registration app_command_init.cpp:286, spelling base_command_interface.hpp:546, case app_command_interface.cpp:1835 (the only case that passes index) -> coreLink.cpp:667-669 -> HipStarMgr::setColorStarTable hip_star_mgr.cpp:131-138, writing the static color_table[128] declared hip_star_mgr.cpp:104; every star is drawn with color_table[its own shade index] at zone_array.cpp:293 and :382 and hip_star_wrapper.hpp:93
names.notes: WHAT THE INDEX SELECTS: one of the 128 slots of the star colour table, keyed on the star's colour index. Slot i stands for B-V = i*(4/127) - 0.5 (IndexToBV, hip_star.hpp:46-49), so slot 0 is B-V -0.5 (hottest, blue) and slot 127 is B-V +3.5 (coolest, red). The slots are filled at startup from the 'colors' section of stars.ini, keys color_000 to color_127 (hip_star_mgr.cpp:112-129). An index outside 0-127 changes nothing and logs 'ColorTable index Error' (hip_star_mgr.cpp:133-135). An omitted index means slot 0, because evalInt of an absent key returns 0 (app_command_interface.cpp:2014 and :4605-4606) - so `color property star_table value 1,0,0` silently repaints the bluest stars red. This is the only colour with no getter at any level (app_command_interface.cpp:1841-1844).

names.name: lunar_eclipse_umbra
names.doc: Meant for the ring of Earth's deep shadow at the Moon's distance, but nothing is drawn, so this has no effect.
names.source: registration app_command_init.cpp:287, spelling base_command_interface.hpp:547, case app_command_interface.cpp:1819 -> coreLink.cpp:142-144 -> SkyLineMgr::setColor skyline_mgr.cpp:144-154; the target class SkyLine_LunarEclipse(UMBRA) exists (factory case skyline_mgr.cpp:427-433, geometry skyline.cpp:1696-1820, umbra radius skyline.cpp:1761-1766) but is never instantiated
names.notes: DEAD AT THIS HEAD. Core builds exactly twenty sky lines at core.cpp:128-149 and neither eclipse type is among them; a search of src/ finds no other skyLineMgr->Create call site. So SkyLineMgr::setColor walks an empty match, logs 'SkyLineMgr error : setColor not found LINE_LUNAR_ECLIPSE_UMBRA' at skyline_mgr.cpp:153 and returns. The script sees success. The matching flag `flag lunar_eclipse_umbra on` is equally inert. Worse for a saved session: the read side, SkyLineMgr::getColor, returns the fallback baseColor for a missing line (skyline_mgr.cpp:164-165) rather than failing, so a session would record a colour that was never anyone's.

names.name: lunar_eclipse_penumbra
names.doc: Meant for the wider ring of Earth's part-shadow at the Moon, but nothing is drawn, so this has no effect.
names.source: registration app_command_init.cpp:288, spelling base_command_interface.hpp:548, case app_command_interface.cpp:1820 -> coreLink.cpp:142-144 -> skyline_mgr.cpp:144-154; the target class SkyLine_LunarEclipse(PENUMBRA) exists (factory case skyline_mgr.cpp:434-440, penumbra radius skyline.cpp:1767-1773) but is never instantiated
names.notes: Same dead path as lunar_eclipse_umbra - see that entry for the full trace.

_suspected_bugs.what: Two registered colours drive an object the engine never builds
_suspected_bugs.source: core.cpp:128-149 (the twenty Create calls) against app_command_init.cpp:287-288, applyColor app_command_interface.cpp:1819-1820, SkyLineMgr::setColor skyline_mgr.cpp:144-154
_suspected_bugs.detail: lunar_eclipse_umbra and lunar_eclipse_penumbra are registered, routed and fully implemented (skyline.cpp:1685-1820), but SkyLineMgr::Create is never called for either type, so the map lookup always misses. setColor logs a warning and returns; the script is told the command succeeded. The paired flags (app_command_init.cpp:228-229) are inert for the same reason.

_suspected_bugs.what: getColor invents a value for a missing line instead of refusing
_suspected_bugs.detail: When the type is absent the getter logs a warning and returns the member baseColor. AppCommandInterface::readColor (app_command_interface.cpp:1935-1940 for the two eclipse types) has no way to tell that apart from a real answer, so a saved session records baseColor as though it were the live colour of a line that does not exist.

_suspected_bugs.what: planet_orbits / planet_names / planet_trails cannot recolour anything already on screen
_suspected_bugs.source: app_command_interface.cpp:1796-1798 -> coreLink.cpp:1471-1473 -> solarsystem_color.cpp:60-62 -> body_color.cpp:82-107, against the constructor at body_color.cpp:14-37 and the draw-time reads at hints.cpp:75, orbit_2d.cpp:54, orbit_3d.cpp:46, trail.cpp:106
_suspected_bugs.detail: The three commands write static defaults that a body reads once, in its constructor. BodyColor::reset (body_color.cpp:42-48) is called from nowhere else, so nothing ever re-applies a changed default to an existing body. A script author who writes `color property planet_orbits value 1,0,0` and sees no change is looking at correct behaviour, which is exactly why it needs saying in the tooltip.

_suspected_bugs.what: galactic_line's object reads uninitialised memory in navigation and astronomical modes
_suspected_bugs.source: src/coreModule/skyline.cpp:943-988 (the extra-circle block) against skyline.cpp:936-942 (where the extra points are filled) and the allocation at skyline.cpp:907
_suspected_bugs.detail: SkyLine_Equator fills points[nb_segment+1 ...] only for the EQUATOR variant, but the drawing block that consumes them runs for any variant whenever internalNav or internalAstronomical is set. For LINE_GALACTIC_EQUATOR that block reads never-written heap. Reported as observed from the source; not reproduced at runtime in this pass.

_suspected_bugs.what: ecliptic_center is a script spelling that contradicts its own drawing
_suspected_bugs.detail: The name promises a centre; the code draws the two ecliptic poles. Frozen-field compatibility makes the spelling unchangeable, so the tooltip is the only place the mismatch can be resolved for a user.

_suspected_bugs.what: The zodiac sign names are printed with a degree sign glued on
_suspected_bugs.detail: oss << zod[...] << "\xc2\xb0" appends the degree character to a constellation name, so the dome shows e.g. LEO followed by a degree symbol. The names are also hardcoded with leading pad spaces (skyline.cpp:242-253) and are never translated.

_suspected_bugs.what: The Greenwich circle is placed at twice the observer's longitude
_suspected_bugs.source: src/coreModule/skyline.cpp:623 (fixed longitude -2 * observer longitude) with the frame convention at observer.cpp:108-114
_suspected_bugs.detail: In the body-fixed frame the true Greenwich meridian is frame longitude 0, so the factor of -2 puts the circle on geographic longitude 2*L. It lands on the real prime meridian only from longitude 0 or 180. Reported as observed from the source; not measured at runtime in this pass.

_suspected_bugs.what: Copy-paste in the sky-line default colours and in one log line
_suspected_bugs.detail: core.cpp:1654-1656 reads LINE_ANALEMMALINE's default colour from the constellation-boundary key, LINE_ANALEMMA's from the constellation-names key and LINE_ARIES's from the constellation-art key. Separately, the LINE_ECLIPTIC factory case logs 'SkyLineMgr creating LINE_MERIDIAN' (skyline_mgr.cpp:421). Neither affects the `color` command, but both mislead anyone reading the log or the defaults.
